claim: Wearing face masks can cause infections from bacteria such as staphylococcus.
justification: The high-confidence evidence (e.g., item 8 with confidence 0.90, corroborated) explicitly states that clinical studies document prolonged mask use increasing Staphylococcus aureus skin colonization and leading to infections. Other corroborated items (2, 3, 4, 10) further support the association between mask-wearing and bacterial colonization that may cause infections. While health authorities (items 7, 11, 17 with high confidence) do not list bacterial infections as a risk, their guidance focuses on mask benefits and does not refute the claim; thus, the evidence strongly implies that wearing face masks can cause staphylococcal infections.
